scope: Primary statistical sources support definitions and cautions, not a numeric accuracy target for a compact jitML recipe

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook: Binomial Distribution
sources.supports: Binomial mass/cumulative probability, fixed success probability; used only for the explicitly stated independent uniform-guessing null

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook: Bonferroni method
sources.supports: General probability inequality for finite predeclared families; arithmetic bound30/3000=.01 or150/3000=.05, without independence between comparisons

sources.title: scikit-learn official r2_score documentation
sources.supports: Held-out mean prediction has zero R-squared for nonconstant targets; constant targets need explicit handling; not a population confidence claim

sources.title: Cawley and Talbot2010: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
sources.supports: Optimizing finite evaluation/model-selection criteria can induce overfitting and biased performance evaluation; criterion versioning does not create fresh test data

inferences_by_reviewer_not_claims_of_sou: Initial-versus-final exact predictive improvement is sufficient for the proposed descriptive benchmark claim when paired with real execution, baseline controls and five-run evidence, not for published-model parity.
A retained stricter historical restriction cannot cause false acceptance of a model failing an independent conjunct, but does not gain independent provenance from that fact.
No statistical source uniquely determines an application utility margin or requires a made-up compact-model accuracy target.
